process_name: BNL - Supply - Supplier Invoicing - MIRO Actions
clean_description: Our Demand & Supply Planning Team gets a large amount of invoices from suppliers on a daily basis. On a yearly basis receive over 35.000 invoices from our suppliers. In very exceptional cases, invoices are processed as .XML file using an EDI connection. In all other cases the processing of the received invoice consists of a series of manual actions.  Processing the received supplier invoices consists of a series of actions that are carried out in our SAP environment. Excluding exceptional cases, a lot of these actions can be seen as repetitive and of little added value. Regardless, these actions need to be carried out continuously and with great care given the impact of this process. Given the repetitive nature of some of these actions, there is little added value to gain from doing them manually. This creates a major opportunity for improvement through standardization and the implementation of automation solutions.  The goal of this project is to standardize and automate the supplier invoicing process for as many suppliers as possible. We try to achieve this using technology and software from different fields of discipline. Invoices that are received from suppliers in the scope of our project will get automatically forwarded to a specific folder that is being monitored by our OCR software Abbyy FlexiCapture Studio 12. New files automatically get examined by our OCR software and all the details important for the invoicing process are stored in an .XLS database. The extracted results are keyed in automatically using an RPA-enhanced process created in the UiPath Studio environment. Manual treatment is only required for exceptions.  After all preliminary checks have been carried out, the remaining validated lines in the .XLSX file are cleared for further processing in SAP. The actual keying in of the invoice details happens in the MIRO transaction of our SAP environment.   For each invoice that needs to be processed a data table will be generated from the details present in the database. Once all lines from a specific invoice/purchase order have been generated in the previously mentioned data table, the first actions in the SAP transaction are carried out. First, the workflow fills in all invoice specific details. Before being able to move on to line specific details, the workflow might have to deal with a couple of pop-ups and other menus.  For example: if the purchase order was a direct delivery, an extra context menu will pop up for this specific purpose. The UiPath workflow needs to be capable to handle all sorts of possible exceptions that might be the case for the invoice it is currently processing.  An extensive exception handling has been added to the workflow in order to deal with all possible exceptions we are currently aware of. This is subject to change as we expand the scope of the project. We will keep on training the workflow to be able to handle all future exceptions as well.

process_name: BNL - MKT/Supply - ME23N - Get purchase price valid at PO Creation time
clean_description: Our Finance department sends a list of blocked invoices to our Marketing department for them to qualify any differences in purchasing price and to validate or reject payment. Our product managers go through the list to see whether the blocked invoice was due to the supplier using the wrong price, data being keyed in wrong in our SAP environment, etc. However, the ZL60 and ZM59 transactions give the purchasing price that is valid at the date of the report. It is possible that the purchase price has changed between the date of the Purchase Order creation and the date of the report.
